title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
main_claim: There is a polynomial-time uniform family of polynomial-size quantum circuits over {NOT, CNOT, Toffoli, H, S, inverses, singly controlled versions} that outputs the complete prime factorization of every N>=2 with probability exactly one.
coverage: Read all sections plus the appendix. Lemma 3.2 (four-phase kickback transform): I simulated the circuit for b=5, and its success-projected matrix equals Q^{-1/2} g(kx/Q) to machine precision. Lemma 3.3 (continued-fraction bin recovery): the inequality 2Q > vB(B-1) holds and the labels are unique. Lemma 4.1 (dyadic majorant): I checked the Lipschitz/Riemann-sum error, the lower bound 2/pi - pi^2/32 > 1/8, the coefficient-rounding error <= 1/Q, the resulting U-P in [32/Q, 97/Q], and S in [1/(128d), 2]. A numerical spot check with Q=2^14 and d<=200 gave max |P-J|*Q ~ 0.17, against the claimed bound of 32. Three-mode completion: the mode masses c*sum P/2 + c*sum(U-P)/2 + rho sum to lambda(d), the bounds c<=1/8 and rho<=2*2^{-10n} hold, and every retention probability lies in [0,1]. Prop 5.1: I checked the 2-adic level counts, the bound F>=phi(m)/2, phi(d)/d>=1/(n+1), s>=1-2^{-2n} (K x >= 2n for n>=128), the gcd split via square roots of 1 modulo odd prime powers, and the tree depth/size bounds (q-1 < (p-1)/2) and slot count <= 6n^7 < L. Section 6: in Lemma 6.1, R*2^W/delta <= 1/4 and the passing masses sum to z; (1-delta)s >= z holds. The identification of the analytical event T with the implemented event A holds pointwise in both directions: T => A by the all-good completion guarantee, and A => T because verification forces D' = D(N) by unique factorization. The chain-rule probability z^L uses fresh registers and coins at each slot. In the quarter lemma, c_* <= 1 and 2^{J+1}e <= 1/4, the one-step reflection algebra gives exactly 2g_*, and the reflection about |psi> is realised as V_N(2|0><0|-I)V_N^{-1}. Appendix (AKS variant): the existence of s via the bound log P_R > n^6, the lower bound 8^{h-1} on the number of distinct values, the upper bound 2^{2n sqrt h} < 2^{2h} for h > n^2, and the existence of a second prime p' for composite non-powers are all valid.
sibling_notes: The family 279 hash was empty when I checked, so there were no sibling reports to cross-reference.
